newsitem.title: USA: HCIA seen recovering from market battering.
newsitem.headline: HCIA seen recovering from market battering.

text.p: HCIA Inc, which had its market value nearly halved on Tuesday, will likely need at a couple of quarters to recover from a sharp earnings shortfall as management refocuses itself on sales to large customers, analysts said .
Because the company's woes did not stem from lack of demand, analysts said, the problems were not a refection of an industry-wide slowdown and could be rectified by measures HCIA said it is adopting.
"I think this is a one- or two-quarter event," said Alex. Brown analyst Ann Gallo.

Recent acquisitions and equity offerings distracted senior HCIA management from leading key sales and marketing efforts, including those to large pharmaceutical and medical device maker customers, the company said.
This led to the revenue shortfall in the third quarter that triggered the bludgeoning of HCIA's stock.
The stock fell 27-1/8, or 45 percent, to 32-7/8, topping Nasdaq's list of most actively traded issues.

Late Monday, the Baltimore-based health care information services company said it expected its third quarter earnings in a $0.10-to-$0.15-per-share range, before a one-time charge, and its fourth quarter results around $0.15 to $0.20 a share.
Analysts had forecast earnings of $0.29 a share for both quarters, according to First Call.
In response to the shortfall, HCIA said it would focus its sales efforts through specific business units and boost the role of senior management in operations and sales efforts.
"The market opportunity in this sector is tremendous," Gallo said. "The problem you're seeing companies have is managing the growth and managing the volatility that comes with growth."
The HCIA profit warning raised investor jitters over the prospects for the healthcare information group after Medaphis Corp in August and Cerner Corp in July issued their own earnings warnings.
Several stocks in the group sold off on Tuesday, but analysts said they did not think the HCIA news was an indication of an industry-wide trend.
"This is a company-specific event," UBS Securities analyst Anthony Vendetti said. "It's not an indication of slowing demand."
